description: All Stream Deck actions in @iracedeck/iracing-plugin-stream-deck with their modes and sub-actions.

modes.label: Incidents
modes.description: Live incident count, flashes on new incident

modes.label: Time Remaining
modes.description: Session time left, flashes when < 5 min

modes.label: Laps
modes.description: Current lap number

modes.label: Position
modes.description: Class (default) or overall race position, optionally shows total cars (scoped to class or full field)

modes.label: iRating Gain/Loss
modes.description: Estimated iRating change for the current race — green for a gain, red for a loss, -- when no estimate is possible

modes.label: Gaps
modes.description: Live crossing-time gap to the car one class position ahead/behind with gaining/losing trend colors (race sessions only)

modes.label: Fuel
modes.description: Fuel level as amount or percentage

modes.label: Laps to Empty
modes.description: Laps the current tank will last — live fuel level divided by the average per-lap consumption over the configurable 1-20 lap window

modes.label: Flags
modes.description: Active race flags with colors and pulsing

modes.label: Track Wetness
modes.description: Track wetness state with a centered vertical 6-segment bar; the current state is the icon title

modes.label: Wind
modes.description: Wind as an arrow pointing where the wind pushes the car with the speed below it; relative-to-car or compass direction, in m/s, km/h, or mph

actions.name: Telemetry Display
actions.description: Custom mustache template display for any telemetry or session variable

actions.name: Audio Controls
actions.description: One audio action for both surfaces (#782). On a KEYPAD button the category/action settings pick one of the modes below. On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only — the Mirabox/Ulanzi manifests declare no dial controllers per #786) the action is a volume dial (settings under the dial root): dial.category picks what rotation adjusts — voice-chat / master / spotter tap the iRacing volume key bindings once per detent (capped per event; iRacing exposes no volume state, so the touch strip shows category identity only; spotter (#809) reuses the AI Spotter Controls spotterLouder / spotterQuieter bindings, surfaced in this action's Related Key Bindings too), race-engineer / radar step iRaceDeck's own 0-100 levels by 5 per detent with a live level bar + value on the touch strip (dimmed OFF state when the feature gate is disabled). dial.pressAction (default none) picks the press: push-to-talk holds audioControlsPushToTalk for the press duration (red ON AIR band while held), mute-unmute taps audioVoiceChatMute for voice-chat, taps spotterSilence for spotter (a blind one-way tap like voice-chat mute), or toggles the Pit Crew feature gate for race-engineer / radar (shared toggle pathway, ack clips included; not offered for master — iRacing has no master-mute keybind). The strip render is Elgato-only (dial feedback flag). The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller).

actions.name: Black Box Selector
actions.description: One black-box action for both surfaces (#808). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks Direct (opens the box chosen by the blackBox setting — a toggle: pressing again while shown closes it), Next, or Previous; each taps a single key binding (blackBoxLapTiming…blackBoxWeather, blackBoxCycleNext, blackBoxCyclePrevious). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: rotation ALWAYS cycles — clockwise taps blackBoxCycleNext, counter-clockwise blackBoxCyclePrevious, scaled by ticks and capped at 5 per event (there is no rotation-setting selector). A press gesture (dial.pressAction/dial.longPressAction, default None, plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction/dial.longTouchAction, default None) can Open Selected Box: it single-taps the per-box binding chosen by dial.pressBox — the SAME single-tap dispatch the keypad Direct mode uses (so it toggles too). iRacing exposes no open-box telemetry (the #782 identity-only compromise), so the touch strip is static: a BB badge + BLACK BOX wordmark, dimmed under the #612 warning when the Cycle bindings are unset; it refreshes on global-settings changes, not telemetry (this surface never subscribes to the tick). Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed fires no gesture. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces (no SDK support).

actions.name: Pit Crew
actions.description: Multi-mode action for the iRaceDeck audio framework: the Race Engineer voice toggle, the directional Radar proximity ticks, and the Corner Names callout toggle (#897). The radar-volume mode moved to the Audio Controls action (#590) — hidden from the Pit Crew Mode dropdown but kept functional so existing buttons keep working.

modes.label: Race Engineer Toggle
modes.description: Flips the Race Engineer master gate (voice scenarios + pit ambience) on/off, with a spoken acknowledgment

modes.label: Radar
modes.description: Toggles the directional proximity tick loop on/off

modes.label: Corner Names
modes.description: Toggles the corner-name callouts (practice/test) on/off — flips the same calloutEnabledCornerNames setting as the PI checkbox, with a spoken acknowledgment (#897)

modes.label: Radar Volume Up
modes.description: Deprecated (#590) — moved to Audio Controls. Hidden from the PI but kept functional. Bumps the global Radar volume by 5 (max 100)

modes.label: Radar Volume Down
modes.description: Deprecated (#590) — moved to Audio Controls. Hidden from the PI but kept functional. Reduces the global Radar volume by 5 (min 0)

actions.name: Cockpit Misc
actions.description: One Cockpit Misc action for both surfaces (#805). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (toggle/trigger wipers, report latency, in-lap mode, and directional dash-page-1/dash-page-2 with a Direction; ffb-max-force is a hidden legacy alias of Force Feedback since #827). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks dash-page-1 or dash-page-2 and turning cycles it via the shared cockpitMiscDashPage* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound; ffb-max-force is intentionally NOT a rotation setting — FFB rotation belongs to the Force Feedback dial). The live page number (dcDashPage/dcDashPage2) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only), showing --- when the car exposes no dash pages. The dial press/long-press and touch gestures are configurable over every keypad one-shot {Toggle Wipers, Trigger Wipers, In-Lap Mode, Report Latency, None}, all defaulting to None. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

modes.label: FFB Max Force Up
modes.note: Legacy alias of Force Feedback ffb-force (#827); kept functional, not selectable in the PI

modes.label: FFB Max Force Down
modes.note: Legacy alias of Force Feedback ffb-force (#827); kept functional, not selectable in the PI

actions.name: Force Feedback
actions.description: One force-feedback action for both surfaces (#802). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks one of the modes below; directional modes take a Direction setting, and everything taps the shared forceFeedback*/cockpitMiscFfbForce* key bindings (FFB Force shares the Cockpit Misc keys, #827). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only — the Mirabox/Ulanzi manifests declare no dial controllers per #786), with settings under the dial root: dial.setting picks one value — ffb-force, wheel-lfe, or bass-shaker-lfe — and turning steps it via the same increase/decrease bindings (clockwise increases; both directions must be bound; scaled by ticks, capped at 5 taps per event). FFB Force shows the live max force (SteeringWheelMaxForceNm, the only value iRacing reports) as "XX.X Nm" in a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip; the two LFE settings have no readback and render label-only (the #782 identity-only compromise). Press gestures — dial.pressAction (default None), dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction / dial.longTouchAction (default None for VR safety) — each over {Auto FFB, None}; Auto FFB taps the forceFeedbackAutoCompute binding (default None because auto-compute overwrites the tuned force — not blind-safe). Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed adjusts the value and fires no press gesture. auto-compute-ffb-force is keypad-only (not a rotation value). SteeringWheelMaxForceNm is not a dc* setup var, so the surface formats it with a local Nm formatter rather than the shared View machinery. Dial logic lives in force-feedback-dial-surface.ts behind a host interface (the Fuel Service pattern). The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Splits & Reference
actions.description: One action for both surfaces (#807). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (cycle with a next/previous Direction, toggle-ref-car, custom-sector-start/end, active-reset-set/run). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) there is a single rotation behaviour, so settings under the dial root are gesture slots only (no dial.setting): turning cycles the splits/delta modes — clockwise taps splitsDeltaNext, counter-clockwise splitsDeltaPrevious, scaled by tick magnitude and capped at 5 taps per event; both bindings must be set. iRacing exposes no telemetry for the selected splits mode, so the self-drawn touch strip is identity-only (a DELTA label, never a value; the #782 compromise) and the surface never subscribes to telemetry. dial.pressAction (default toggle-ref-car), dial.longPressAction, dial.tapAction, dial.longTouchAction each pick one of every keypad one-shot mode — toggle-ref-car (taps toggleUiDisplayRefCar), custom-sector-start (splitsDeltaCustomSectorStart), custom-sector-end (splitsDeltaCustomSectorEnd), active-reset-set (splitsDeltaActiveResetSet), active-reset-run (splitsDeltaActiveResetRun) — or none; press/long-press/push+turn are classified at dialUp (no timer), so the dial gesture slots stay momentary taps even for active-reset-run. On the KEYPAD every mode taps its binding once EXCEPT active-reset-run, which holds it (HOLD_MODES, the Car Control HOLD_CONTROLS shape) and releases on keyUp / willDisappear (#1028). The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

modes.label: Cycle Delta Mode
modes.description: Cycles through splits delta display modes (next/previous via direction setting)

modes.label: Toggle Reference Car
modes.description: Toggles the reference car display on/off

modes.label: Custom Sector Start
modes.description: Marks the start point for a custom sector

modes.label: Custom Sector End
modes.description: Marks the end point for a custom sector

modes.label: Set Active Reset Point
modes.description: Saves the current car state as a reset snapshot (solo practice only)

modes.label: Reset to Start Point
modes.description: Teleports the car back to the saved active reset snapshot (solo practice only). The ONLY mode that holds its binding (#1028): pressed on keyDown, released on keyUp, so holding the key keeps the sim paused at the reset point. A short press is equivalent to the old tap.

modes.label: Take Snapshot
modes.description: Developer tool: saves the current telemetry + session info to disk as timestamped JSON and Markdown files

actions.name: View Adjustment
actions.description: One view action for both surfaces (#806). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (fov/horizon/driver-height/ui-size with a Direction, plus the non-directional recenter-vr and mouse-to-sim one-shots). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks fov/horizon/driver-height/ui-size and turning steps it via the shared viewAdjust* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound). iRacing exposes no telemetry for any of these values, so the self-drawn touch strip (Elgato only) shows the setting's label only — no value, no readback (the #782 identity-only compromise). Press gestures: dial.pressAction (default Recenter VR, which is blind-safe and the exact gesture a VR driver wants) and dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction/dial.longTouchAction (default None), each over {Recenter VR, Mouse to Sim, None}; Recenter VR taps the viewAdjustRecenterVr binding, Mouse to Sim runs the same native window/pointer call as the keypad mode. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed fires no gesture. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). The non-directional mouse-to-sim keypad mode (#926) focuses the iRacing window (regardless of the focusIRacingWindow global setting — pressing the key is explicit intent) and moves the OS mouse pointer to the client area at 50% x / 12.5% y, via deck-core's window service; it issues NO iRacing command, so it has no key binding, no comms descriptor, and never shows the #612 warning. Communication: key bindings on both surfaces, except mouse-to-sim (no iRacing command).

modes.label: Jump to Fastest Lap
modes.description: Jump the replay cursor to the fastest lap of either the viewed car or always your own car (session-scoped; no dial support)

modes.label: Next Car (Number Order)
modes.description: Switch camera to next car by number order (includes pit cars, excludes the pace car and cars no longer in the sim world, #885)

modes.label: Previous Car (Number Order)
modes.description: Switch camera to previous car by number order (includes pit cars, excludes the pace car and cars no longer in the sim world, #885)

actions.name: Camera Editor Adjustments
actions.description: One camera-editor action for both surfaces (#804). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks one of 15 modes (14 directional camera-tool parameters with a Direction, plus the non-directional Auto Set Mic Gain), each tapping a camEdit* key binding. On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks one of the 14 rotatable parameters (latitude/longitude/altitude, yaw/pitch, fov-zoom/f-number/focus-depth, vanish-x/vanish-y, blimp-radius/blimp-velocity, key-step, mic-gain) and turning steps it via the shared camEdit* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound). iRacing exposes NO camera-tool telemetry, so every parameter is identity-only: the self-drawn dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only) shows the parameter's full name only, never a live value. Press gestures: dial.pressAction/dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction/dial.longTouchAction (default None for VR safety), each over {None, Auto Set Mic Gain, and every Camera Editor Controls one-shot — the camCtrl* keys reused verbatim (#804)}; Auto Set Mic Gain taps camEditAutoSetMicGain and each camera-tool one-shot taps its camCtrl* binding. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed fires no gesture. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Camera Controls
actions.description: One camera action for both surfaces (#803). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks one of the modes below — camera-group changes, camera/sub-camera/car/driving cycling (with a Direction setting and a per-action camera-group subset for Cycle Camera), and focus targets (your car, leader, incident, most exciting, position, car number, camera state, plus the Elgato-only Focus Car pick-from-grid). Every mode is an iRacing SDK camera command (getCommands().camera.*) with two exceptions: Cycle Sub-Camera taps iRacing's own Next / Previous Sub Camera key bindings, because the switch broadcasts' camera argument never selects a sub-camera (#852; preconfigured to B / Shift+B, so it works without setup); and the Elgato-only Focus Car pick-from-grid mode (focus-select-car), whose press is a deck-side switch to the Car Selector profile rather than a camera command. Apart from the sub-camera pair there are no key bindings and nothing to configure. On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only — the Mirabox/Ulanzi manifests declare no dial controllers per #786) the settings live under the dial root: dial.mode picks the target (camera, sub-camera, car-number, race-position, track-order, driving; default car-number — the pre-rework 'car' value migrates to car-number via a schema preprocess). Rotation moves one step per detent — the turn direction replaces the keypad's Direction setting: clockwise = next for the LIST modes (camera / sub-camera / driving), while the NUMBER-PRIMARY modes are flipped (MODE_NUMBER_PRIMARY = race-position #884 + car-number #973: a clockwise detent makes the number on the strip go DOWN — P4 → P3, #94 → #77 — so one rule covers both; track-order is a car mode but NOT number-primary, since its next already IS the car ahead on the road, so it lands on the car ahead clockwise without a flip), and the dial.reverseRotation checkbox (default false) inverts the active mode's mapping (checked on a number-primary mode = the pre-flip feel, where clockwise raises the number; deliberately NO migration for either flip, since the flag is per-dial and the user can change dial.mode afterwards): the cycle modes (camera/sub-camera/driving) reuse the keypad's own executeCycle dispatch, while car-number, race-position, and track-order focus the nearest present car along an explicit ordering (ascending car number; the canonical getLiveRacePositions order per race-positions.md with official CarIdxPosition as the documented fallback; or — track-order, #886 — the physical road order via the shared findNearestCarOnTrack primitive wrapped by computeTrackOrderTarget in shared/car-cycling.ts, filtered to the same competitor set as car-number so the pace car and spectators are never targeted), walking past cars no longer in the sim world so a post-race towed/exited car with a frozen rank cannot dead-loop the cycle (#885, shared with the keypad Cycle Car mode; track-order uses the primitive's own lap-distance + track-surface in-world test), via the keypad Switch by Car Number command (camera.switchNum) (race-position resolves its target to a car number too, never a bare position, so the previewed and switched-to car agree). The touch strip (a single full-cell pixmap, Elgato only) always names the MODE on its small top line (CAMERA / SUB-CAMERA / CAR # / POSITION / TRACK ORDER / DRIVING CAM); below it the main content is a CAROUSEL of what that mode acts on: Cycle Camera shows the current camera group's icon (from CAMERA_SELECT_ICONS, the enabled global cameraGroupSubset) with its name and the dimmed prev/next groups either side; Cycle Sub-Camera shows the current camera's NAME within the focused group (from CameraInfo.Groups[].Cameras[] via getCamerasInGroup + computeSubCameraCarousel — the SAME carousel the sub-camera dispatch steps through, so preview == execution incl. wrap) flanked by the adjacent cameras; the car modes show the focused car number (CamCarIdx + driver list) flanked by the neighbouring numbers, with a P<pos> badge in race-position mode and AHEAD / BEHIND captions under the side numbers in track-order mode (dropped when both detents resolve to the same car) — every mode's side previews follow the EFFECTIVE mapping (left = the counter-clockwise detent's target, right = the clockwise one; #884), so preview == execution holds under the number-primary default flip and the reverse option; Cycle Driving Camera shows the current group icon+name ONLY (driving hands group ± 1 to iRacing to resolve and wrap, so there is no coherent neighbour to preview — none beats a lying one) — all in a per-mode color-coded dash box, falling back to a mode-identity label out of session, refreshed on telemetry ticks and throttled to ≤10/s. Cycle Camera's dial PI shows the same camera-groups checkbox grid the keypad uses, bound to the global cameraGroupSubset. Five gesture-value options across four slots — dial.pressAction, dial.longPressAction, plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction / dial.longTouchAction — each over {Focus My Car, Change Camera, Focus on Leader, Focus on Incident, Focus on Most Exciting, None}, all default None (blind-safe rule); every gesture reuses the matching keypad SDK camera dispatch. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp (no timer); turning while pressed cycles and fires no press gesture. Dial logic lives in camera-dial-surface.ts behind a host interface (the Fuel Service pattern); the shared camera-group subset walk lives in camera-groups.ts. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller): keypad instances see the Mode + per-mode settings and appearance sections, dial instances the dial settings. Communication: iRacing API on both surfaces, except Cycle Sub-Camera — the keypad mode and the dial's sub-camera mode both tap the cameraControlsSubCameraNext/Previous key bindings (#852).

modes.label: Focus Car (pick from grid)
modes.description: Opens the iRaceDeck Car Selector profile with a focus intent — pressing a car key focuses the camera on that car and stays on the grid (Elgato Stream Deck only).

actions.name: Fuel Service
actions.description: One fuel action for both surfaces (#759). On a KEYPAD button the Mode setting picks one of the eight modes below; every fuel value goes through the iRacing API (pit.fuel against the live PitSvFuel baseline — no chat macros): Add/Reduce Fuel send pit.fuel(round(PitSvFuel ± amount)), Set Fuel Amount sends the absolute amount, a target at or below zero empties the request (1 L then clearFuel). The shared unit setting is auto | l | g | k, default Auto (from iRacing's live DisplayUnits); kilograms convert via sessionInfo DriverInfo.DriverCarFuelKgPerLtr (skipped with a warning when unavailable); legacy pre-#759 instances with a persisted mode but no unit are migrated to liters and the migration is persisted back so the PI shows it, while fresh instances persist auto on their first appear (before the PI can save a mode) so the two shapes stay unambiguous. Add/Reduce support hold-to-repeat (~250 ms cadence). The enableFuelingOnChange global ('Auto-enable fueling') is KEYPAD-ONLY: when off and fueling is off, adjustments send pit.fuel then pit.clearFuel to restore the unchecked box. On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only — the Mirabox/Ulanzi manifests declare no dial controllers per #786) the action is the full fuel dial (former Fuel Dial action, settings under the dial root): modal by live telemetry — in MANUAL mode a bare turn sets the fuel to add (dial.mode chooses Add Amount or Target Amount, the target kept topped up as fuel burns while fueling is on, red target line on the bar); in AUTOFUEL mode a bare turn adjusts the autofuel lap margin via the fuelServiceLapMarginIncrease/Decrease key bindings (coalesced); AUTOFUEL: N/A when unavailable. Five gesture slots (dial.pressAction default Toggle Fueling, dial.longPressAction default Toggle Autofuel, dial.pushTurnAction Full / No Fuel pair default None, plus Elgato-only dial.tapAction / dial.longTouchAction default None for VR safety) each over Toggle Fueling, Toggle Full / No Fuel, Toggle Autofuel, Switch Mode, None. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp (no timer); the self-drawn 200x100 touch strip carries the REFUEL/AUTOFUEL status band, per-mode readout, and two-segment fuel bar, refreshing every 5 s and immediately on displayed-state changes. The dial always auto-arms fueling on rotate (deliberately ignores enableFuelingOnChange). The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller): keypad instances see the mode settings, dial instances the dial settings; the dial Unit select omits kilograms.

modes.label: Change All Tires
modes.description: Request all four tire changes using the iRacing #t pit chat macro

modes.label: Toggle Tires
modes.description: Per-wheel selection: LF, RF, LR, RR. Uses shorthand macros (#!t, #!l, #!r) when all, left-only, or right-only tires are selected

modes.label: Change Compound
modes.description: Cycle tire compounds (DRY/WET)

actions.name: Setup Brakes
actions.description: One brake action for both surfaces (#775). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks one of the modes below (six live-telemetry View sub-modes with optional dual-press, seven adjustments with a Direction setting); everything taps the shared setupBrakes* key bindings. On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only — the Mirabox/Ulanzi manifests declare no dial controllers per #786) the action is the former Setup Brakes Dial (#730), with settings under the dial root: dial.setting picks one brake value — brake bias, brake bias fine, peak brake bias, brake misc, engine braking, or ABS adjust — and turning steps it via the same increase/decrease bindings (clockwise increases; both directions must be bound). The live telemetry value (dcBrakeBias/dcBrakeBiasFine/dcPeakBrakeBias/dcBrakeMisc/dcEngineBraking/dcABS) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box — a short label (BB/BBF/PEAK/MISC/ENG/ABS) plus a large number, no % sign — on the touch strip (a single full-cell pixmap, Elgato only). Press gestures — dial.pressAction (default Toggle ABS), dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction / dial.longTouchAction (default None for VR safety) — each over {Toggle ABS, None}; Toggle ABS taps the setupBrakesAbsToggle binding. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed adjusts the value and fires no press gesture. No View modes on the dial (the display shows the value) and no ABS Toggle rotation mode. Dial logic lives in setup-brakes-dial-surface.ts behind a host interface (the Fuel Service pattern). The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller): keypad instances see the Mode/Direction/dual-press and appearance sections, dial instances the dial settings; the Related Key Bindings section is shared. Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Setup Chassis
actions.description: One chassis action for both surfaces (#800). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (View sub-modes plus the differential/ARB/spring/shock/power-steering adjustments with a Direction). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks one of the 13 components and turning steps it via the shared setupChassis* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound). The live value (dcDiffPreload/dcDiffEntry/dcDiffMiddle/dcDiffExit/dcAntiRollFront/dcAntiRollRear/dcPowerSteering) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only); the springs and shocks have no dc* telemetry, so they rotate but show the label only. Setup Chassis has no toggle, so the dial press does nothing and no touch gestures are offered. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Setup Aero
actions.description: One aero action for both surfaces (#799). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (View sub-modes, front-wing/rear-wing/qualifying-tape adjustments with a Direction, and the RF Brake Attached toggle). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks front-wing, rear-wing, or qualifying-tape and turning steps it via the shared setupAero* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound). The live value (dcFrontWing/dcRearWing) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only); qualifying-tape has no dc* telemetry, so it rotates but shows the label only. Press gestures: dial.pressAction/dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction/dial.longTouchAction (default None for VR safety), each over {Toggle RF Brake, None}; Toggle RF Brake taps the setupAeroRfBrakeAttached binding. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed fires no gesture. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Setup Engine
actions.description: One engine action for both surfaces (#798). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (View sub-modes plus engine-power/throttle-shaping/boost-level/launch-rpm adjustments with a Direction). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks one value and turning steps it via the shared setupEngine* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound). The live value (dcEnginePower/dcThrottleShape/dcLaunchRPM) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only); boost-level has no dc* telemetry, so it rotates but shows the label only. Setup Engine has no toggle, so the dial press does nothing and no touch gestures are offered. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Setup Fuel
actions.description: One in-car fuel action for both surfaces (#797) - distinct from Fuel Service, which controls pit fueling. On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (View sub-modes, fuel-mixture/fuel-cut-position adjustments with a Direction, and the disable-fuel-cut/low-fuel-accept/fcy-mode-toggle one-shots). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks fuel-mixture or fuel-cut-position and turning steps it via the shared setupFuel* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound), with the live value (dcFuelMixture/dcFuelCutPosition) as a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only). Press gestures: dial.pressAction/dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction/dial.longTouchAction (default None for VR safety), each over {Toggle FCY Mode, None}; Toggle FCY Mode taps the setupFuelFcyModeToggle binding. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed fires no gesture. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Setup Hybrid
actions.description: One hybrid/ERS action for both surfaces (#796). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (View sub-modes, the MGU-K deploy-mode/regen-gain/fixed-deploy adjustments with a Direction, and the HYS hold controls). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks MGU-K deploy mode, regen gain, or fixed deploy and turning steps it via the shared setupHybrid* increase/decrease bindings (both directions must be bound). The live value (dcMGUKDeployMode/dcMGUKRegenGain/dcMGUKDeployFixed) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box on the touch strip (Elgato only). Setup Hybrid has no single toggle, so the dial press does nothing and no touch gestures are offered. Press vs long-press would be classified at dialUp. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.

actions.name: Setup Traction
actions.description: One traction-control action for both surfaces (#795). On a KEYPAD button the Mode dropdown picks a mode below (four View sub-modes TC1-TC4, the TC Toggle, and the TC1-TC4 slot adjustments with a Direction). On a DIAL (Elgato Encoder only - the Mirabox/Ulanzi manifests declare no dial controllers per #786) settings live under the dial root: dial.setting picks one TC slot (TC1-TC4) and turning steps it via the shared setupTraction* increase/decrease bindings (clockwise increases; both directions must be bound). The live value (dcTractionControl/dcTractionControl2/dcTractionControl3/dcTractionControl4) renders as a self-drawn color-coded dash box (short label plus a large number) on the touch strip (Elgato only). Press gestures: dial.pressAction (default Toggle TC), dial.longPressAction (default None), plus the Elgato-only dial.tapAction/dial.longTouchAction (default None for VR safety), each over {Toggle TC, None}; Toggle TC taps the setupTractionTcToggle binding. Press vs long-press is classified at dialUp; turning while pressed fires no gesture. The PI branches per controller (actionInfo.payload.controller). Communication: key bindings on both surfaces.
